trigger: Confirmed security incident affecting customer data
deadline: Without undue delay and within 48 hours of confirmation; 24 hours for the 38 Enterprise customers with negotiated terms; status updates at least every 72 hours
notify: Each affected customer's security contact, then the customer administrator
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, all customers. Plan to the 24-hour clock
owner: VP Customer Support with the General Counsel

obligation: Business associate notice under the BAA
citation: BAA with each of the 46 covered entities (contract)
trigger: Security incident or breach of unsecured PHI involving healthcare cell data
deadline: Within 10 business days of discovery (shorter than the 60-day legal limit)
notify: Each affected covered entity's privacy or security contact

obligation: HIPAA breach risk assessment by a business associate (four factors)
trigger: Acquisition, access, use, or disclosure of PHI not permitted by the Privacy Rule
deadline: Before deciding a notice is not needed; document as soon as the scope is known
notify: Internal decision log (shared with the covered entity under the BAA)
clock_starts: Presumed a breach unless the assessment shows a low probability of compromise

obligation: HIPAA business associate notice to the covered entity
trigger: Discovery of a breach of unsecured PHI
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery; include, to the extent possible, the identification of each individual and other information the covered entity needs for its notices
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - business associate for 46 covered entities
clock_starts: Discovery: first day known, or by reasonable diligence would have been known, to any employee, officer, or agent other than the person committing the breach (164.410(a)(2))

trigger: A law enforcement official states that notice would impede a criminal investigation or damage national security
deadline: Written statement: delay for the period specified. Oral statement: document it and delay no longer than 30 days unless confirmed in writing

obligation: HIPAA burden of proof and records
trigger: Any use or disclosure in violation of the Privacy Rule
deadline: Keep records that show every notice was made or that the event was not a breach (company retains 6 years, POL-01 4.14)

trigger: Computer-security incident that has materially disrupted or degraded, or is reasonably likely to materially disrupt or degrade, covered services to a banking organization customer for 4 or more hours (not scheduled maintenance previously communicated)
deadline: As soon as possible after the company determines it has experienced such an incident
notify: At least one bank-designated point of contact at each affected bank; if none was provided, the bank's CEO and CIO or two individuals of comparable responsibility
applies_at_this_tier: Yes for the 9 community bank customers. Whether the platform is a "covered service" under the Bank Service Company Act is a legal judgment; counsel treats it as covered, and the bank contracts require the notice in any case
clock_starts: Company determination that the incident meets the 4-hour test

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the covered entity
trigger: Breach of security of a system the company maintains for a customer, involving personal information of Florida residents as defined in 501.171(1)(g)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 10 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred; give the customer the information it needs for its own notices
notify: Each affected customer (the covered entity), which then gives notice under 501.171(3) and (4)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if Florida personal information is involved (about 6 million Florida end-consumer records on the platform). Counsel decides per data element
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred

obligation: California service provider notice to the data owner (worked example of another state)
trigger: The company maintains computerized data it does not own, and California residents' personal information (as defined in 1798.82(h)) was, or is reasonably believed to have been, acquired by an unauthorized person
notify: Owner or licensee of the data (each affected customer)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if California personal information was acquired (about 11 million California end-consumer records). Other states have similar service-provider duties; counsel checks each state where affected individuals reside

obligation: State data breach notification to residents
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI, Guam)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of state residents (definitions vary by state)
deadline: Varies by state (for example "without unreasonable delay" or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where required; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: For customer data, customers own the data and usually give resident notices; the company supports them under the DPA. For company-owned data, the company notifies. Apply the law of each state where affected individuals reside

obligation: Florida breach notice to individuals (company-owned data)
trigger: Breach of personal information the company owns (for example customer administrator credentials or its own employees' data) of Florida residents
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 30 days after determination. Not required if, after investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the company reasonably determines in writing that identity theft or other financial harm is not likely; keep that determination 5 years and send it to the Department of Legal Affairs within 30 days (501.171(4)(c))
applies_at_this_tier: Only for data the company owns
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida where the company is the covered entity
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 30 days after determination (the 15-day good-cause extension applies only to notice to individuals, not to this notice)
applies_at_this_tier: Only as covered entity (company-owned data) and 500 or more Floridians

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
applies_at_this_tier: Only as covered entity and more than 1,000 individuals

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom or extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (2021-09-21); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering any payment to a threat actor
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); law enforcement or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: All U.S. persons; strict liability. POL-03 4.8 also requires CEO, counsel, and insurer approval

trigger: Suspected security incident or outage that may lead to a claim
deadline: Through the carrier hotline before engaging incident vendors

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports (pending final rule)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment by a covered entity
deadline: 72 hours (covered incident); 24 hours (ransom payment) - not yet effective
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; recheck the covered-entity criteria for IT sector SaaS providers when it is final

trigger: Breach of CPNI held by a telecommunications carrier or interconnected VoIP provider
deadline: As soon as practicable, no later than 7 business days after reasonable determination; customers only after 7 full business days post-LE notice (unless urgent/LE directs otherwise)
notify: USSS and FBI via FCC central reporting facility; then customers
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company offers no voice service and is not a carrier or interconnected VoIP provider

obligation: Form 8-K Item 1.05 material cybersecurity incident disclosure
trigger: Registrant determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: Within four business days after determining the incident is material
applies_at_this_tier: No - privately held. The PE sponsor's own reporting duties, if any, are handled by the sponsor
